title: Local SEO: Google's 3 Ranking Factors and What It Costs
desc: Google says local results rest on relevance, distance and prominence, and that no one can pay for a better rank. What local SEO tools and services cost in 2026.
keywords: local seo, local seo services, google business profile optimization, local seo pricing, local seo cost, google local ranking factors, google business profile
cta: Want help showing up in local search?
body:
Short answer. Google says local results are "mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity," and that "there's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking." The Business Profile that feeds those results is free. What you can pay for is software and help: at the three vendors we checked (Whitespark, Moz and BrightLocal), local SEO tools start at $1 a month per location and managed services at $499 a month. We read every source below on 11 November 2026.

This guide is for a small business owner who wants to show up when someone nearby searches for what they sell. It covers what Google itself says decides local ranking, the Business Profile steps Google recommends, the rules that can get a profile suspended, and what local SEO tools and services cost. If you want the wider picture of agency SEO fees, see our guide to SEO pricing.

What local SEO is

Local SEO is the work of getting a business to appear in Google's local results: the map listings on Search and the results inside Google Maps. Google describes the trigger in its Business Profile help page on local ranking: when a customer searches for a business or place near their location, they find local results on Maps and Search. Its own example is someone searching "Italian restaurant" on their phone.

The listing in those results comes from your Google Business Profile. Google's product page calls it a "free Business Profile," and setting one up costs nothing. The paid side of local SEO is the time, the tools and any outside help you use to keep that profile complete, earn reviews and build the links and citations that make a business better known.

Google's three local ranking factors

Google says it does its best to keep the algorithm details confidential, but it names the factors. The help page opens the section by saying local results are "mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity," then explains them under three headings: relevance, distance and prominence.

FactorHow Google defines itWhat you can change
RelevanceHow well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching forComplete, detailed business info and the right category
DistanceHow far each business is from the person searchingLittle: your address or service area must be accurate
ProminenceHow well known a business is, including how many websites link to it and how many reviews it hasReviews, ratings, links and mentions across the web

Two details in Google's wording matter. On distance, Google says that if a searcher does not share where they are, "Google uses what it knows about their location." On prominence, Google says "more reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking," and that the factor is also based on "how many websites link to your business."

The same page states plainly that there is "no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google." So treat any offer of a promised map position with care: Google says the ranking itself is not for sale.

The Business Profile steps Google recommends

Google's local ranking page lists these actions:

  1. Verify your business. Google says verification "tells Google that you're authorized to represent the business, so it's more likely to show up in search results."
  2. Keep your information complete and accurate. Google says "businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results." It names your full address if customers can visit you, your hours including special store hours, your business category, and attributes such as parking or Wi-Fi.
  3. Respond to reviews. Google says replying "shows that you value their feedback," and that positive reviews and helpful replies can help a business stand out.
  4. Add photos and videos that show what you offer.
  5. Add in-store products if you run a retail store. Google says this is available only for retail businesses in eligible countries or regions.

Verification has its own help page. Google picks the method for you: "Verification methods are automatically determined by Google and can't be changed." The options it lists are phone or text, email, a live video call and mail. After you finish, Google says verification reviews "take up to 5 business days," and on rare occasions longer. A profile can be verified instantly in some cases, for example when you have already verified your website in Google Search Console.

Google's profile rules to know

Google's guidelines for representing your business set the limits. Four rules are worth knowing before you edit your profile:

  • Your real name only. The name "should reflect your business's real-world name, as used consistently on your storefront, website, stationery, and as known to customers." Google says "including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted, and could result in the suspension of your Business Profile." We read that as ruling out a city or a service keyword added to the name.
  • Few categories. Google asks you to "choose the fewest number of categories it takes to describe your overall core business."
  • One profile per business. Google says "there should only be one profile per business," because more than one can cause problems with how your information displays on Maps and Search.
  • No virtual offices for service-area businesses. A plumber or cleaner who travels to customers should have one profile for the central office with a designated service area, and Google says service-area businesses "can't list a 'virtual' office."

Google adds that it reserves the right to suspend access to Business Profiles for businesses that break these guidelines.

Reviews: what Google and the FTC do not allow

Reviews feed the prominence factor, which makes them the place where shortcuts are most tempting. Google's Maps content policy treats "reviews or ratings that have been paid for, directly or in kind" as fake engagement, and it does not allow merchants to offer incentives, "such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services," in exchange for posting any review or for removing a negative one. That covers a discount for a five-star review, and also a discount for any review at all.

In the United States there is also federal law. The FTC announced a final rule in August 2024 that bans the sale or purchase of fake reviews, including AI-generated fake reviews, and lets the agency seek civil penalties against knowing violators. It also bans compensation or other incentives conditioned on a review expressing a particular sentiment, positive or negative. The rule is 16 CFR Part 465, published in the Federal Register on August 22, 2024; the FTC said it would take effect 60 days after publication, which works out to October 21, 2024. This is general information, not legal advice.

A pattern that stays inside both sets of rules, in our view: ask customers for honest reviews with no reward attached, and reply to the reviews you get.

What local SEO tools cost

We checked three local SEO vendors that publish prices on their own sites. These are their published list prices in USD, read on 11 November 2026; per-location prices are for one location.

Vendor and planListed priceWhat the plan covers
Whitespark Local Platform$1 a month per locationBusiness Profile management, bulk edits, preventing unwanted updates
Whitespark Local Rank Tracker$14 to $200 a monthLocal rank tracking
Whitespark Reputation Builder$79 a month per locationAutomated review requests and review management
Moz Local Lite$199 a year ($16 a month)90+ listing directories, Local Grid map pack ranking, review monitoring
Moz Local Elite$399 a year ($33 a month)Includes the Listings AI add-on, more social channels and a reporting suite
BrightLocal Track$41 a month, or $369 a yearRank tracking for up to 100 keywords and four competitors, audits, citation monitoring
BrightLocal Grow$65 a month, or $584 a yearAdds review monitoring and review requests by email, SMS and in store (listing sync and post scheduling come with the $54 Manage plan)

Paying yearly is cheaper at BrightLocal. BrightLocal Track costs $492 over 12 monthly payments against $369 billed annually, a $123 difference that matches the saving BrightLocal shows. BrightLocal also sells citations one at a time: its pricing page says Citation Builder starts at $3.20 per site, or as low as $2 with bulk credits, with no plan needed. Note that BrightLocal says its platform works in the USA, UK, Canada and Australia.

As a hypothetical, a single-location business that pairs Moz Local Lite with Whitespark's Local Platform would pay $199 plus $12, or $211 a year, at these list prices. That buys Moz Local Lite's listings and review monitoring plus Whitespark's profile management. It does not write review replies, take photos or fix a wrong category for you.

What local SEO services cost

When you hand the work to someone else, the published prices jump. BrightLocal's managed SEO service is listed "from $499" a month. Whitespark lists its done-for-you SEO service at $499 to $1,999 a month, and one-time listing work at $20 to $999. Over a year, $499 a month is $5,988 and $1,999 a month is $23,988.

Those are two vendors' list prices, not a market average. For survey figures on what SEO agencies charge in general, our SEO pricing guide covers the published numbers. Whatever you pay, we suggest asking any provider which of Google's three factors their work targets, and what they will do on your profile, your reviews and your links each month.

Local SEO and AI answers

Local results now show up beyond the map pack too. As we covered in our piece on Google AI Mode for home services, Google has added booking and quote links for some home services inside AI Mode. We expect the same basics, accurate business details, real reviews and mentions on other sites, to help there. Our guide on getting ChatGPT to recommend your business covers that side.

Calls from a map listing are leads, so plan who answers them. If chat is part of that plan, our guide to AI chatbot costs for small businesses lists what those tools charge.

faqs: How much does local SEO cost?

The Google Business Profile itself is free. At the three vendors we checked on 11 November 2026, tools run from $1 a month per location (Whitespark Local Platform) to $200 a month (the top Whitespark Local Rank Tracker plan), with all-in-one plans such as BrightLocal Track at $41 a month. Managed local SEO is listed from $499 a month at BrightLocal and at $499 to $1,999 a month at Whitespark.
What are the 3 local ranking factors on Google?

Google names relevance, distance and prominence. Relevance is how well a profile matches the search, distance is how far the business is from the searcher, and prominence is how well known it is, including links and reviews.
Can I pay Google for a better map ranking?
No. Google's help page says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google.
Can I put keywords in my Google Business Profile name?

Google says the name should reflect your real-world business name, and that including unnecessary information in it is not permitted and could result in suspension of the profile. We read that as ruling out added keywords or city names.
How long does Google Business Profile verification take?
Google says verification reviews take up to 5 business days, and on rare occasions longer. Some profiles are verified instantly, for example when the website is already verified in Search Console.
Can I offer a discount for Google reviews?

No. Google's Maps policy does not allow incentives such as payment, discounts or free goods in exchange for posting any review. In the US, the FTC's rule at 16 CFR Part 465 also bans incentives conditioned on a positive or negative review.
